sentences.text: Herasmius is smaller than the genus Heterosteus and possesses a comparatively broader and shorter skull.
The type species Herasmius granulatus was described in 1966 by Ørvig based on an incomplete skull found in early Eifelian-aged freshwater deposits on Spitsbergen, Norway.
The species Herasmius dayi was described in 2017 by Schultze and Cumbaa from Lower Devonian marine deposits in the Bear Rock Formation, Canada.
Herasmius belongs to the parent group Dunkleosteidae.
Herasmius is classified within the class Placodermi.
Fossils of Herasmius have been found in freshwater deposits in Norway and Canada.
Herasmius lived during the Eifelian stage, between 393.47 and 390.5 million years ago.
